chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassha' from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Do not eat from vessels of gold and silver."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating from gold and silver vessels in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the prohibition (*haram*) of eating and drinking from gold and silver vessels, a ruling derived from the direct command of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). In Shia jurisprudence, this is often linked to the concept of *israf* (extravagance) and distinguishing the elite from the common in pre-Islamic times, serving as a marker of modesty and spiritual humility. The chain of narration highlights the transmission of this etiquette through prominent figures like al-Wasshash and Dawud ibn Sirhan, underscoring its acceptance in early Shia legal circles.
